title: XDIP: A Curated X-ray Absorption Spectrum Dataset for Iron-Containing Proteins
experiments_summary: The paper describes a semi-automated dataset construction pipeline and several validation/benchmarking experiments: (1) Literature search using keyword combinations (e.g., 'XAS Protein', 'EXAFS Metalloprotein') across multiple publishers, yielding 20,915 articles screened down to 573 relevant publications. (2) Manual digitization of XAS spectra (XANES and EXAFS) from published figures using WebPlotDigitizer V4, with careful axis calibration, color recognition distance tuning (2, 5, or 10 pixels), and manual curve tracing. All spectra were interpolated to a uniform 100-point length. (3) Manual structural annotation of iron-centered local protein environments, recording atom types, 3D Cartesian coordinates, adjacency matrices, bond lengths, bond angles, and sourcing structures from PDB, CCDC, SMILES, or manual reconstruction. (4) Annotation accuracy validation: 50 synthetic XANES and 25 synthetic EXAFS plots were generated using Fe-based data from the Materials Project with varied shape ratios, curve counts, and line styles, then anonymously inserted into each of four experts' annotation workloads. Annotated spectra were linearly interpolated to reference x-values and compared using Mean Squared Error (MSE). (5) Inter-rater reliability assessment using Intra-class Correlation Coefficient (ICC) computed across all four experts on the same synthetic dataset, averaged over interpolated spectral points. (6) Forward modeling benchmark: Three GNN architectures (GCN, GAT, GIN) were trained to predict 100-point XAS spectra from local atomic structure graphs, using an 80/10/10 train/validation/test split with stratification, AdamW optimizer, learning rate 1e-3 with plateau scheduler, up to 300 epochs with early stopping, and evaluated by MAE. (7) Inverse modeling benchmark: MLP and Random Forest models were trained to predict coordination number (classification) and mean nearest-neighbor distance (regression) from 100-point XAS vectors, using the same data split and training framework, evaluated by accuracy, Macro-F1, and MAE.
